# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity

> [!NOTE]
>
> The upcoming SDK 10, CLI 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases require an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs with uploads disabled. These versions must ship after the backend run-start endpoint is deployed. Earlier versions keep their existing behavior.

`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.

Results are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) event, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the run adds no telemetry of its own.

## Eval identity and local data

Run `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `apiKey` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the saved CLI login. An invalid explicit credential never falls back to another account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an organization admin for a key if you cannot create one.

Every logical run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior successful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the project using its existing `--project`, environment, and linked-project settings; a key can only access its own organization.

With results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, project selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executors). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-run request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs. MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the model, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no debit, quota draw, or balance refusal.

`DO_NOT_TRACK`, `MCPJAM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable analytics, not the required run-start request. Results remain local unless result uploading is enabled separately.

  passThreshold: 1
  validity: {}

The hosted app uses a daily credit system to power AI features like chat.

* **Guests** get a free daily usage allowance. Higher-priced models are greyed out in the model picker with a "Sign in to use this model" tooltip — sign in to unlock them. The sidebar shows a progress bar with how much of your daily limit you've used and when it resets. When you reach the limit, you'll be prompted to sign in.
* **Guest session limit**: The hosted app creates a guest session the first time you visit from a given network. If too many guest sessions have been created from your network in a single day, a banner appears: "Too many guest sessions from your network today. Sign in to continue." Signing in removes this restriction.
* **Signed-in users** get **10×** the daily usage of a guest. Your daily usage and any paid credit balance are visible in the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar.
* **Paid credits** can be topped up from the billing page and are shown alongside your daily limit in the account menu.
* **Low credits warning** — when your credit balance drops to 10% or below, the sidebar credit meter turns red and shows a **Low credits** label.
* **When credits run out**, only the free hosted models are locked. Models you access with your own API key (BYOK) remain available regardless of your credit balance.

When your credit balance reaches zero, free models are grayed out in the model picker so you can see the limit before sending a message. Models from your own API keys remain available. If you have paid top-up credits, free models stay enabled even after your daily free allowance is exhausted.

## Signing out

Open the **account menu** at the bottom of the sidebar (click your avatar or email) and choose **Sign out**. You'll be returned to the public app as a guest, and any signed-in usage allowance is replaced by the guest allowance until you sign back in.
--

## Billing

### Payment history

The **Payment history** card on the org billing page lists your recent credit top-ups. Each row shows:

| Column | Details |
| - | - |
| Date | When the top-up was processed |
--

To add credits, click **Top up** — either from the empty state when you have no history, or from the credit balance card above.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Free plan organizations cannot purchase credits directly.** If your organization is on the Free plan, the Top up dialog shows a message that only an organization owner can upgrade the plan, with a **Compare plans** button. Clicking it closes the dialog and opens your organization's Plans settings so you can upgrade.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Desktop app:** When you confirm a top-up in the desktop app, checkout opens in your default system browser and the dialog closes automatically. Your credit balance updates in the app once the purchase completes — no redirect back into the app is required.

### Spend budget

An owner or admin can cap what the whole organization spends on MCPJam-billed
work — chat, evals, judges and computer time — for each billing period, from
**Organization → Budget**.

* Set the cap in dollars, and choose the percentages to be warned at. The
  default warns at 80%; reaching the cap always notifies, whether or not you
--
  are refused for the whole organization. The refusal says the budget is
  reached and that an owner or admin can raise it — buying credits does not
  clear it. Work already in flight finishes, and running computers keep going
